hero.headline: St. Lucie County school bus driver arrested after second student comes forward with allegations
hero.body:

The arrest marks an escalation in a case that initially involved one student. Authorities confirmed that a second alleged victim has provided information to investigators, leading to the driver's detention. The charges involve conduct alleged to have occurred while the individual was employed as a school bus driver in St. Lucie County.

The case has raised immediate concerns among parents and school officials across St. Lucie County, where the driver transported students as part of regular school routes. The school district has not released specific details about which schools or routes were affected, but parents with children who rode district buses have been alerted to the arrest. Law enforcement continues to investigate whether additional victims may exist.

The driver remains in custody as the investigation proceeds. Authorities have not disclosed the ages of the alleged victims or the specific timeline of the incidents. The St. Lucie County School District is cooperating with law enforcement as the case moves forward through the criminal justice system. Parents seeking information about the case or their children's bus routes have been directed to contact the school district directly.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce downtown parking enforcement now issuing citations after two hours
cards.body:
Downtown Fort Pierce visitors now face parking citations if they leave their vehicles in public spaces for more than two hours. The city has begun enforcing the time limits with hefty fines for violators who exceed the posted restrictions.

The parking enforcement affects all guests visiting downtown Fort Pierce businesses, restaurants, and waterfront attractions. City officials have implemented the policy to improve parking turnover in the downtown district, where available spaces have become scarce during peak business hours. The citations carry substantial fines for residents and visitors who fail to move their vehicles within the two-hour window.

Downtown business owners and regular customers will need to adjust their routines to comply with the new enforcement. The policy impacts anyone spending extended time in the downtown area, including employees, shoppers making multiple stops, and diners enjoying leisurely meals. Visitors attending events or conducting business downtown should plan to relocate their vehicles or face potential fines.

The city has not announced grace periods or warnings for first-time violators. Fort Pierce joins other Treasure Coast municipalities in actively managing downtown parking to balance business access with available spaces. Residents planning visits to downtown Fort Pierce should monitor parking times and be prepared to move vehicles before the two-hour limit expires to avoid citations.

cards.headline: Jupiter launches first-ever fire department with 91 firefighters sworn in
cards.teaser: Jupiter made history Monday as 91 firefighters took the oath to launch the town's first municipal fire department.
cards.body:
Ninety-one firefighters and their families gathered at the Maltz Jupiter Theatre on Monday for a historic ceremony launching Jupiter Fire Rescue. The town officially established its first-ever municipal fire department, marking a significant change in emergency services for Jupiter residents.

The new Jupiter Fire Rescue replaces the previous fire service arrangement for the town. All 91 firefighters took their oaths during the ceremony at the local theater. The launch of the municipal department represents a major shift in how fire and emergency services will be provided to Jupiter going forward.

hero.headline: New Martin County dispatch center ready to coordinate Sheriff's Office and Fire Rescue operations
hero.body:
Martin County has completed a new dispatch center that will coordinate emergency operations for the Martin County Sheriff's Office and Fire Rescue. The facility is described as the brain of the county's emergency response system.

The dispatch center serves as the central hub for coordinating all emergency calls and deploying first responders across Martin County. The facility handles 911 calls and dispatches both law enforcement and fire rescue personnel to incidents throughout the county's communities including Stuart, Jensen Beach, Palm City, Hobe Sound, and Port Salerno.

The new center represents a significant upgrade to the county's emergency response infrastructure. Dispatch centers process incoming emergency calls, coordinate the deployment of deputies and firefighters, and maintain communication with first responders in the field during active incidents. The facility consolidates these critical functions in a modern operation center designed to handle the county's emergency services needs.

The completion of the dispatch center comes as Martin County continues to grow and requires more sophisticated emergency response coordination. The Sheriff's Office and Fire Rescue will operate from the unified dispatch facility, improving communication and response times across the county. Officials have confirmed the center is now operational and ready to serve residents.

cards.teaser: First responders worked the scene of a vehicle crash on Florida's Turnpike in Martin County that caused injuries and traffic delays.

Emergency crews responded to a vehicle crash on Florida's Turnpike in Martin County that resulted in injuries. First responders arrived at the scene to provide medical assistance and manage the incident.

The crash caused traffic delays on the turnpike as crews worked to clear the scene and assist injured motorists. Florida's Turnpike runs through Martin County connecting communities to points north and south.

cards.headline: Martin County property value growth declines for fourth consecutive year
cards.teaser: Property value growth in Martin County has declined for four years in a row, according to new data.

Property values impact county tax revenues that fund local services including schools, roads, and public safety. The continued decline in growth rates represents a significant shift from the rapid appreciation Martin County properties experienced in earlier years.

The Susan B. Anthony Award honors individuals who have made significant contributions to voter education and civic involvement in Martin County. The League of Women Voters is a nonpartisan organization focused on voter registration, education, and advocacy.

The combined brewery and distillery represents a new type of alcohol production facility for Martin County. The business model allows patrons to sample both craft beer and locally distilled spirits at one location.

hero.body:
Jose Tsu Zamora, 64, was arrested after an attempted armed kidnapping at First United Methodist Church on SW Prima Vista Boulevard in Port St. Lucie. The incident occurred at the church, prompting a police response and investigation.

Zamora now faces multiple felony charges in connection with the attempted kidnapping. Authorities have not released details about the victim or what led to the incident at the church. The case remains under investigation by Port St. Lucie police.

cards.teaser: St. Lucie County officials are discussing plans to establish a rocket recovery facility at the Port of Fort Pierce for major space companies.

St. Lucie County is considering plans to turn the Port of Fort Pierce into a rocket recovery facility for SpaceX and Blue Origin. County officials discussed the proposal, which would make the local port a hub for recovering rocket components used by the space companies.

The facility would bring new economic activity to Fort Pierce and St. Lucie County. Officials are working through the details of how the port could accommodate the rocket recovery operations. The proposal represents a potential expansion of the port's role in Florida's space industry.

cards.body:
Edwin Garcia, 72, of Port St. Lucie faces an additional battery charge after a second victim came forward with information for investigators. The former St. Lucie County school bus driver was arrested on May 28 on the new charge.

Garcia had previously faced charges related to another alleged victim. The second victim provided additional information to authorities, leading to the new arrest. The cases involve allegations against Garcia during his time as a school bus driver in St. Lucie County. The investigation continues as authorities work through the allegations from both victims.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie daughter charged with attempted murder, arson after setting house fire with mother inside
cards.teaser: A Port St.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie woman faces attempted murder and arson charges after allegedly setting her mother's house on fire while her mother was inside. Michelle Picard, 26, was arrested following the incident after investigators determined she intentionally started the blaze.

The victim first noticed smoke coming from underneath her bedroom door. When she opened the door, she discovered Picard standing nearby. The investigation revealed the fire was deliberately set, leading authorities to charge Picard with attempted murder in addition to arson. The mother escaped the fire without serious injury.

Port St. Lucie police arrested Picard after their investigation into the house fire. The incident marks a serious case of domestic violence in the city. Authorities have not released additional details about what may have prompted the alleged attack or the extent of damage to the home.

Picard remains in custody facing multiple felony charges. The attempted murder charge carries severe penalties under Florida law. The case will proceed through the St. Lucie County court system. Police have not indicated whether additional charges may be filed as the investigation continues.

hero.headline: Demolition begins at Indian River County mall, Macy's store first to go
hero.body:
Demolition work has begun at a Florida mall in Indian River County, with the former Macy's store slated as the first building to be torn down. The project marks a significant transformation for the retail property that has served the local community for years.

The demolition represents a major change for the shopping center and surrounding area. The Macy's store closure and subsequent demolition follows a pattern of retail consolidation affecting communities across the Treasure Coast.

The timeline for completing the full demolition has not been disclosed, though work crews have already mobilized at the site. Property owners and developers have begun the process of removing the anchor store building, which will be followed by additional demolition work on other portions of the mall complex in coming months.

Indian River County residents who frequented the mall and Macy's location will see substantial changes to the retail landscape in their community. The demolition project will likely take several months to complete, with construction equipment and increased truck traffic expected in the area during that time. County officials are monitoring the project to ensure proper permits and safety protocols are followed throughout the demolition process.

cards.headline: Good Samaritan rescues boaters after vessel sinks in Indian River Lagoon
cards.teaser: A Good Samaritan pulled boaters to safety after their vessel sank in the Indian River Lagoon.
cards.body:
Boaters were rescued by a Good Samaritan after their boat sank in the Indian River Lagoon. All passengers made it to safety thanks to the quick response of another boater who witnessed the vessel going down and pulled the occupants from the water.

The rescued boaters expressed gratitude that everyone survived the incident. The sinking occurred in the lagoon waters, a popular boating area for Treasure Coast residents. Details about what caused the vessel to sink have not been released, and marine authorities may investigate the incident to determine the cause of the sinking.

cards.headline: Drone deployment adds 3.5 million clams to Indian River Lagoon restoration effort
cards.teaser: A drone deployment operation has added 3.5 million clams to the Indian River Lagoon as part of ongoing restoration efforts.
cards.body:
Restoration crews have used drones to deploy 3.5 million clams into the Indian River Lagoon, pushing the environmental recovery project past a major milestone. The aerial deployment method allows for efficient distribution of juvenile clams across targeted areas of the lagoon ecosystem.

The massive clam deployment represents a significant step in efforts to restore water quality and ecological health to the Indian River Lagoon. Clams act as natural water filters, with each organism capable of filtering large volumes of water daily. The milestone deployment brings the total number of clams introduced to the lagoon to a substantial figure as restoration partners work to reverse decades of environmental degradation.
